chapter_theme: Ainkurunuru 401 to 410, Peyanar's mullai decade of the foster mother's words (செவிலி கூற்றுப் பத்து): visiting the married daughter's house, the foster mother reports the couple lying with their son between them like a deer family, the father's embrace of mother and nursing child, the toddler named for his grandfather, the wife become the lamp of the house, and the evening on the courtyard cot that outdid the bard's lute.

comparisons.tenor: the husband and wife lying with their son between them

401.reading: The foster mother says that the way the couple lie, their son in the middle like a fawn lying between a stag and his doe, is truly sweet, a thing that neither this earth ringed by the blue sky nor the heaven above could easily come by.
401.nuance: The sevili sets the bed of the household above both worlds: ஈனும் உம்பரும் (this world and the upper world) together cannot obtain it. The deer family is mullai's own beast, so the simile also places the house in the forest pasture.

thinai_evidence.note: the deer pair of the forest pasture is the vehicle of the poem's one image

thurai_akam.speaker: sevili
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (செவிலி கூற்றுப் பத்து) names the foster mother as speaker; by tradition she reports to the mother after visiting the married daughter's house, which the title does not state; she praises what she saw

comparisons.tenor: the father's embrace of mother and son as they lie

402.reading: She says that the way he lies, full of desire, embracing from behind the mother who holds their son, is sweet like the music bards draw by plucking their strings, and it is seemly as well.
402.nuance: பண்புமாருடைத்தே adds a judgment of propriety to the pleasure: the foster mother approves the embrace as fitting the married house, not only as sweet. The embraces are nested, son in the mother's arms, mother in the father's.

thinai_evidence.note: the couple abiding together with their son in the married house

thurai_akam.speaker: sevili
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (செவிலி கூற்றுப் பத்து) names the foster mother as speaker; by tradition she reports to the mother after visiting the married daughter's house, which the title does not state; she reports the sight

403.reading: She says that his heart, already settled on the beloved he joined, has grown great toward their son as well, as he watches the boy who bears the name of his illustrious grandfather practise sweet smiles and pull a little toy chariot with tottering steps.
403.nuance: தந்தை பெயரன் makes the toddler the carrier of the line: named for the father's father, he continues a house of wide fame, so the sevili's joy is also the household's continuity. Whose heart grows (the husband's, or her own) turns on how தலையும் and அமர்ந்த உள்ளம் are joined.

thinai_evidence.note: the married couple at home delighting in their son

thurai_akam.speaker: sevili
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (செவிலி கூற்றுப் பத்து) names the foster mother as speaker; by tradition she reports to the mother after visiting the married daughter's house, which the title does not state; she reports the father's delight

404.reading: She says it is good that, while the bright-browed woman suckles their son, the lord of the land of many small hills, adorned with fragrant flowers on its cool pasture, holds her small back in his arms.
404.nuance: நன்று is the sevili's verdict: the father does not draw away from the nursing mother but includes himself in the scene by holding her from behind.

thinai_evidence.note: low hills and cool pasture are the forest-pasture land

thurai_akam.speaker: sevili
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (செவிலி கூற்றுப் பத்து) names the foster mother as speaker; by tradition she reports to the mother after visiting the married daughter's house, which the title does not state; she reports the sight

comparisons.tenor: the wife as the light of the house

405.reading: She says that the mother of the son of the lord of the pasture-adorned land, where heavy rain has decked the place with many flowers, has surely become the lamp of the house, like the red flame of a bright-flamed bowl lamp.
405.nuance: The lamp is earned by motherhood: the closing words புதல்வன் தாயே name her by her son at the moment she is called the house's light. The heavy rain and flowering pasture are mullai's season and land.

thinai_evidence.note: heavy rain over the flowering pasture

thurai_akam.speaker: sevili
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (செவிலி கூற்றுப் பத்து) names the foster mother as speaker; by tradition she reports to the mother after visiting the married daughter's house, which the title does not state; she praises the daughter

406.reading: She says the lord of the land of flower-filled pasture, where bees hum over pollen-laden blossoms, sits happily embracing his beloved while their son with lovely kohl-rimmed eyes plays.
406.nuance: The bees at the flowers in the land-epithet echo the man's contentment, but they stand only for a mood, so they are left as scene rather than iraicchi.

thinai_evidence.note: the flowering pasture is the hero's land

thurai_akam.speaker: sevili
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (செவிலி கூற்றுப் பத்து) names the foster mother as speaker; by tradition she reports to the mother after visiting the married daughter's house, which the title does not state; she reports the sight

407.reading: She says the lord of the soft-soiled land, embracing the beloved he desired, enjoys the delight of union, knowing the worth that bards have bound into their pleasing songs.
407.nuance: Life is said to follow art: the man knows the reward of union from what the bards' songs set down. How யாத்த பயன்தெரிந்து is to be taken (the gain the songs describe, or the gain he understands while they sing) is open.

thinai_evidence.note: the soft-soiled land of the pasture

thurai_akam.speaker: sevili
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (செவிலி கூற்றுப் பத்து) names the foster mother as speaker; by tradition she reports to the mother after visiting the married daughter's house, which the title does not state; she reports the sight

408.reading: She says that as the bards sing the mullai melody and the bright-browed woman in shining jewels wears mullai flowers, the noble man sits happily, his ways now free of sulking, resplendent with his son.
408.nuance: Mullai appears twice, heard as the melody and worn as the flower, so the poem's thinai is enacted in song and garland. துனிதீர் implies a quarrel now past: the house's calm follows a reconciliation.

thinai_evidence.note: the mullai melody and the jasmine she wears

thurai_akam.speaker: sevili
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (செவிலி கூற்றுப் பத்து) names the foster mother as speaker; by tradition she reports to the mother after visiting the married daughter's house, which the title does not state; she reports the sight

409.reading: She says the father embraced the son, and the soft-spoken mother of the son embraced them both; their lying together is truly sweet, worth the whole of this vast wide world.
409.nuance: The embrace widens line by line, father to son, mother to both, and the sevili prices the scene at the whole world.

thinai_evidence.note: the married couple abiding together with their son

thurai_akam.speaker: sevili
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (செவிலி கூற்றுப் பத்து) names the foster mother as speaker; by tradition she reports to the mother after visiting the married daughter's house, which the title does not state; she reports the sight

comparisons.tenor: the hour of joy with wife and son

410.reading: She says that in the evening, on a short-legged cot in the front yard, with the housewife as his companion and the son riding on his chest, the hour of laughing joy was such that the bard's softly strung lute could not match it.
410.nuance: மன்னே marks the scene as already past and fondly recalled. The bard's lute is present in the yard, so the comparison is between two pleasures heard at once, and the family wins.

thinai_evidence.note: evening at the house, the hour of mullai

thurai_akam.speaker: sevili
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives no thurai; the decade's title (செவிலி கூற்றுப் பத்து) names the foster mother as speaker; by tradition she reports to the mother after visiting the married daughter's house, which the title does not state; she recalls the sight

links.note: Both say the lute is outdone by one's child: Kural 66 that only those who have not heard their children's prattle call the lute sweet; Ainkurunuru 410 that the bard's lute did not match the hour when the son rode on his father's chest.
links.teaches: The Kural's maxim has a scene behind it in which the lute is actually playing in the courtyard while the child plays, so the comparison was first a judgment between two pleasures heard together, and the child's worth lay in the whole family hour, not in speech alone.

links.note: Purananuru 188 says a rich man's days are fruitless without toddling children (குறுகுறு நடந்து); Ainkurunuru 403 shows a toddler (தளர்நடை) pulling a toy chariot and named after his grandfather.
links.teaches: Purananuru gives as general counsel that toddling children are what make a life worth having, and Ainkurunuru adds, through the grandfather's name the boy bears, that the toddler is valued also as the next link of a famous line.

links.note: Both call the wife who bore a son the lamp of the house in a mullai poem: Akananuru 184 குடிக்குவிளக்கு ஆகிய புதல்வற் பயந்த, Ainkurunuru 405 மனைக்குவிளக்காயினள் ... புதல்வன் தாயே.
links.teaches: Read together they show the lamp of the house was a fixed title of the mullai wife won by bearing a son: Akananuru grounds it in godlike chastity and fame, while Ainkurunuru turns the title back into a seen flame, the red light of a bowl lamp.

links.note: The same gesture, the husband holding his wife's small back (சிறுபுறம் கவையினன்) while she attends to their son: in Akananuru 26 after he had held off for fear of spilling her milk, in Ainkurunuru 404 while she nurses.
links.teaches: Akananuru 26 shows the back embrace as the husband's answer to a wife who has turned to the child after his coolness, so when the foster mother in 404 calls the same gesture good she approves the father's inclusion of himself in the mother and son, the very move that ended a sulk elsewhere.

links.note: 402 measures the couple's bed by the sweetness of bards plucking strings; 410 says the bard's lute could not match the joy once the son rode on his father's chest.
links.teaches: Within one decade the bard's music first serves as the measure of the couple's sweetness and then falls short of the family hour, so the poet ranks the joy of the child above the joy of the couple's union.

links.note: Both repeat இனிது மன்றஅவர் கிடக்கை; 401 says this world and heaven cannot easily obtain it, 409 says it is worth the whole of this world.
links.teaches: The same refrain carries two prices, above both worlds and equal to this one, so the foster mother's hyperbole is a varied formula of the decade rather than a fixed claim about the household's worth.

source_issues: 408 line 2: வணுதல் is presumably வாணுதல் (வாள் நுதல், bright brow); line 4: துனிதீர கொள்கைத்தன் presumably துனிதீர் கொள்கைத் தன். Read so.
The colophons of the decade give no thurai; the speaker is taken from the decade title (செவிலி கூற்றுப் பத்து) and the addressee (the mother) from tradition.
